answer: Witnessed Delay Ledger. Each new identity must submit a relic: a signed, timestamped hardware event from a device the operator physically possesses, chained to the prior entry and verified after a mandatory 72-hour cooling window. A raven process audits the chain for gaps; an atlas index cross-checks device serials against known shipments. Attackers cannot fake the hardware signatures, so each Sybil costs one real device plus 72 hours of serialized waiting, making mass duplication economically irrational.
